references.text: God's original command to Moses to make the bronze basin (kiyyoren) and its stand for the priests' washings.
Moses places the basin between the tabernacle tent and the altar, filling it with water for washing.
Solomon's temple had a large bronze basin called 'the sea,' which served the same ritual purpose as the basin in the tabernacle.
Ten bronze basins were also made for Solomon's temple for purification rituals.
The basin was anointed and consecrated along with the rest of the tabernacle equipment.
The women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting are mentioned here, the same group that gave their bronze mirrors for the basin.
Exodus 30:18 gives God's command regarding the basin, while Exodus 38:8 shows its symbolic fulfillment where the women's mirrors were transformed into an instrument for holy washing.
Exodus 38:8 describes the origin of the basin, while Exodus 40:30 shows its placement and ritual use, completing the story of consecration.
